comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory NRV Write-Downs Mechanics and Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2023, the company recorded inventory write-downs to NRV due to declining ASPs for DRAM and NAND; these pre-recorded charges resulted in lower subsequent cost of goods sold when the inventory was sold, with the net impact reflecting current period write-downs offset by lower costs from prior period written-down inventory.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose specific accounting charges affecting their Cost of Sales related to excess capacity and inventory valuation. Intel reported $695 million in higher period charges in 2023 primarily for excess capacity and intersegment inventory reserves, which partially offset the decrease in cost of sales from lower volume. Similarly, Micron disclosed that its gross margin was impacted by charges in 2023 to write down inventories to net realizable value (NRV) due to declining average selling prices for DRAM and NAND. Both companies explicitly note that these inventory-related charges in prior periods resulted in lower costs of goods sold in subsequent periods when the inventory was sold.

sentences.text: These cost of sales decreases were partially offset by $695 million of higher period charges in 2023, primarily related to excess capacity charges and higher intersegment inventory reserves taken in 2023.

Inventory NRV write-downs: Our consolidated gross margin was impacted by charges in 2023 to write down inventories to their estimated NRV as a result of declines in average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND.
As charges to write down inventories are recorded in advance of when inventories are sold, costs of goods sold in subsequent periods were lower than they otherwise would be.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company charges cost of sales for inventory provisions to write-down inventory to the lower of cost or net realizable value, or for obsolete or excess inventory. Most provisions relate to excess quantities based on inventory levels and future commitments compared to assumptions about future demand, requiring management judgment.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA discuss inventory provisions charged to cost of sales to adjust inventory values. Intel's 2023 cost of sales included higher intersegment inventory reserves. NVIDIA states that it charges cost of sales for inventory provisions to write down inventory to the lower of cost or net realizable value, noting that most provisions relate to excess quantities based on management's judgment regarding future demand.

sentences.text: These cost of sales decreases were partially offset by $695 million of higher period charges in 2023, primarily related to excess capacity charges and higher intersegment inventory reserves taken in 2023.

We charge cost of sales for inventory provisions to write-down our inventory to the lower of cost or net realizable value or for obsolete or excess inventory, and for excess product purchase commitments.

Most of our inventory provisions relate to excess quantities of products or components, based on our inventory levels and future product purchase commitments compared to assumptions about future demand and market conditions, which requires management judgment.
